newsitem.title: POLAND: Nomura says Polish bourse faces profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Nomura says Polish bourse faces profit-taking.

text.p: The Warsaw Stock Exchange is vulnerable to selling pressure as international investors start taking profits, Nomura Equity Research said in its October East European Monthly report.

"We expect this (selling) to happen gradually as dedicated East European funds who were generally first in the market start off the trend, followed by more recent arrivals such as global emerging market funds and general European funds and finally local retail investors," the report dated September 30 said. @
Nomura said that though Polish firms published "reasonably good" monthly earnings reports over the summer, weak first-half results would still weigh heavily against their full-year performance.
"As a result the market's valuation is already relatively high," the report said.
The Warsaw bourse's main market closed at 14,893.1 points on Monday, up more than 90 percent this year.
